extracted.intended_audience: scientists, science journalists, and the general public interested in science communication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rationale for timing and handling media announcements of scientific results, especially the use and justification of journal press embargoes. Useful for scientists, press officers and journalists deciding when and how to announce findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay public announcement until peer-reviewed publication / respect journal embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists and authors should not publicly announce or speak with the press about a submitted paper until the journal permits it (e.g., Nature prohibits authors from speaking with the press about a submitted paper until the week before publication, and then only under conditions set by the journal). LIGO timed their news conferences and media outreach to coincide with the official publication in Physical Review Letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat journal embargo dates as the appropriate time to broadly announce results; coordinate news conferences and media outreach to coincide with official publication unless the journal explicitly releases authors from embargo. Failure to respect embargoes can undermine the quid pro quo of publication and lead to problems with journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use peer review and publication as the quid pro quo for public claims (priority vs disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific publishing presents a quid pro quo: authors claim priority for results and in return provide detailed disclosure (experimental design, data, reasoning) that allows others to build on, replicate, and confirm the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News coverage alone is not an adequate substitute for the published paper; without the paper and underlying data the public and other scientists cannot act on or evaluate the claim. Announcing results only in the press provides a claim without the substantive disclosure that justifies priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoes protect the public from misinformation and premature claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Press embargoes help prevent the public (and policymakers, clinicians, other scientists) from acting on or being misled by unvetted or incorrect findings — as illustrated by the 2014 gravitational-wave claim later shown to be dust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on peer review to catch errors or overinterpretations before results become widely publicized; avoid 'breaking' unvetted claims because they may later be corrected or reinterpreted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoes allow multiple journalists an equal chance to produce balanced coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing advance copies under embargo gives multiple reporters the opportunity to read the scientific article, seek outside experts, and prepare carefully researched and balanced stories rather than rushed or sensational accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respecting embargoes increases the overall quality and quantity of coverage; reporters benefiting from embargoed access should use the lead time to consult experts and craft nuanced stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the public and practitioners (e.g., doctors) have access to the original paper near the time of news
rubrics_metrics.description: When news stories bias toward 'newsworthiness', having the original scientific article available close to the news story helps prevent exaggeration or misunderstanding, especially for health-related findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate release so clinicians and other professionals can read the study before or at the same time as popular coverage, reducing the chance of premature clinical responses to sensationalized news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoes protect scientists' claims to priority and manage competitive publication dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: An embargo can help protect an author's priority claim; if a competing paper makes news, journals may release their authors from embargo and rush publications, potentially causing the original team to lose the priority race.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embargoed coordinated publication to establish clear priority via journal publication dates rather than relying on informal or premature media announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepublication peer review benefits: time for additional experiments or analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepublication peer review often requires additional experiments or analyses before publication; embargoes allow this process to proceed without external pressure from premature news coverage demanding immediate data or conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid letting news pressure force the disclosure of incomplete data or rush revisions; journals may decline publication if the peer-review process is compromised by publicity-driven demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal policies can set specific restrictions on prepublication communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual journals set concrete rules about author communication (for example, Nature's specific prohibition until a week before publication and conditional allowances).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult and follow the specific communication and embargo policies of the target journal when planning outreach or press releases; different journals have different rules and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint servers are changing the embargo dynamic
rubrics_metrics.description: The advent of preprint servers (e.g., arXiv) allows researchers to share findings before journal acceptance, which is evolving how embargoes and timing of public announcements operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that posting on preprint servers may alter expectations about news timing and the meaning of 'publication'; plan communication strategies accordingly and understand the journal's stance on preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalists and scientists should avoid breaking embargoes; it's unnecessary to serve the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Talking about discoveries in advance of scientific publication is unlikely to help the public; journalists can still create compelling, accurate stories while respecting embargoes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat 'breaking' embargoed science as inherently beneficial; instead, use the embargo lead time to craft accurate narratives and contextualize findings without prematurely releasing unvetted claims.
